title: Load Shape and the Small Business Electricity Supply Renewal Rate: Training Questions
content:
**Load-shape adjustment.** For a Small Business Electricity Supply renewal accepted on or before the contract end date, the largest kWh billed on any one energy line of the agreement is divided by the average kWh per energy line posted in the 12 months before the handling date; a ratio of 1.20 or less takes 0.08 cents per kWh off the renewal rate; a ratio above 1.40 adds 0.10 cents; a ratio above 1.20 and up to 1.40 changes nothing.

**Which line gives the largest kWh?**
The largest kWh billed on any one energy line of the agreement, from all of the agreement's energy lines, not only those of the last 12 months.

**How is the average taken?**
The kWh of the agreement's energy lines posted in the 12 months before the handling date, divided by the number of those energy lines; a line falls in those 12 months when fewer than 12 whole months separate its posted date from the handling date. When no energy line was posted in those 12 months, no ratio is taken and nothing changes.

**What does each ratio do?**

| Ratio of the largest line to the 12-month average | Effect on the renewal rate |
|---|---|
| 1.20 or less | 0.08 cents per kWh off |
| above 1.20 and up to 1.40 | no change |
| above 1.40 | 0.10 cents per kWh added |

**Is exactly 1.20 or exactly 1.40 a change?**
A ratio of exactly 1.20 takes 0.08 cents off; a ratio of exactly 1.40 changes nothing; only a ratio above 1.40 adds 0.10 cents.

**Worked on hypothetical figures**

| Energy lines in the 12 months | Average per line | Largest line ever billed | Ratio | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 lines, 96000 kWh | 8000 | 9500 | 1.1875 | 0.08 cents off |
| 12 lines, 96000 kWh | 8000 | 10400 | 1.30 | no change |
| 12 lines, 96000 kWh | 8000 | 12400 | 1.55 | 0.10 cents added |
